headline_en: Taniya never got to join her Italy-based husband with their child
summary_en: Taniya Afroz (28), wife of an Italy-based Bangladeshi, was travelling from Khulna to Dhaka with her mother on 1 Sep 2024 to collect papers her husband had sent so she and their daughter could join him in Italy, when a bus-truck collision in Kashiani, Gopalganj killed six people including both women. The husband was flying home for the burial.

facts.statement: Aslam Uddin Kuddus, a Bangladeshi living in Italy for a long time, sent the necessary papers from Italy so his wife Taniya Afroz (28) and their 9-year-old daughter could join him in Italy; Taniya was travelling from Khulna to Dhaka to collect those papers.

On Sunday 1 Sep 2024 at about 7:45 am a bus of Imad Paribahan from Khulna collided head-on with a truck on the Dhaka-Khulna highway at Majhigati, Kashiani upazila, Gopalganj; six died, including Taniya Afroz (28), wife of an Italy-based migrant, and her mother Tahura Begum (55); 25 passengers were injured.
facts.source_in_article: Kashiani police SI Md. Selim Mia; relatives and police

facts.statement: Aslam Uddin had returned to Italy two to two and a half months earlier after leave; on hearing of the deaths he set out from Italy, and the burial was to take place after he arrived in Bangladesh.

people_cases.what_happened: Travelling to Dhaka to collect family-reunion papers sent by husband in Italy; died in bus-truck crash in Kashiani, Gopalganj, along with her mother
people_cases.outcome: Died at Faridpur Medical College Hospital

headline_en: 26 Bangladeshis win Commonwealth scholarships this year, welcomed by UK High Commissioner Sarah Cooke
summary_en: 26 Bangladeshis received 2024 Commonwealth Scholarships for master's study at UK universities including Oxford, Cambridge, SOAS, Warwick and Edinburgh. The British Council held a pre-departure briefing at the British High Commissioner's residence on 26 Aug 2024. Since 1960, 1,867 Bangladeshis have received Commonwealth scholarships or fellowships; 105 are currently studying.

facts.statement: In 2024, 26 Bangladeshis received Commonwealth Scholarships for postgraduate (master's) study at UK universities including Oxford University, Cambridge University, SOAS University of London, University of Warwick and University of Edinburgh.
facts.source_in_article: British Council press release; UK High Commissioner Sarah Cooke

facts.statement: The British Council organised a pre-departure briefing session for 2024 Bangladeshi Commonwealth scholars on Monday 26 Aug 2024 at the British High Commissioner's residence in Dhaka, giving essential information and guidance on studying in the UK.

Since the Commonwealth Scholarship programme began in 1960, a total of 1,867 Bangladeshi citizens have received UK-government-funded Commonwealth scholarships or fellowships through the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission (CSC); 105 Bangladeshis are currently studying on Commonwealth scholarships, including the 2023 batch.
Every Commonwealth Scholarship scheme is highly competitive and candidates need an outstanding academic record to succeed.

Subjects of 2024 Bangladeshi Commonwealth scholars include behavioural and economic science, biological chemistry, civil engineering, computational applied mathematics, data and decision analytics, education, electronic and electrical engineering, environmental science, GIS, global health policy, global health science and epidemiology, healthcare management, human rights, international development law and human rights, international relations law, management, medical statistics and health data science, museum studies, public health, public policy, sustainable agriculture and food security, and textiles and apparel.

summary_en: An opinion piece by Rahman Mridha, former Pfizer director in Sweden, on Bangladesh's image, economy and challenges. It says the economy depends heavily on remittances and that more than 1.5 crore Bangladeshis work abroad. The rest covers border issues, exports, governance and youth.

headline_en: Europe-bound students at risk as Indian visa operations halt
summary_en: A reader piece (Aug 2024) says Bangladeshi students admitted to universities in European countries with no embassy in Bangladesh must take visa interviews in India, but the Indian Visa Application Centre (IVAC) suspended visa operations indefinitely after the July-August 2024 unrest. Students who paid tuition risk cancelled admission if they miss embassy interviews by 15-20 September, and refunds often lose 30-40%. Workers bound for those countries are also affected.

facts.statement: Portugal, Bulgaria, Romania, Lithuania, Hungary, Austria and other European countries have no embassy in Bangladesh, so Bangladeshi students going to study there must give their visa interview in neighbouring India.
More than 300 Bangladeshi students go each academic year to study in these European countries (those without embassies in Bangladesh).

In August 2024 the Indian Visa Application Centre (IVAC) in Bangladesh suspended visa operations indefinitely; a week before the 20 Aug 2024 article IVAC announced limited operations on its website but was not accepting any visa forms, only returning previously submitted passports, and most students emailing got no reply.
Students who cannot attend embassy visa interviews (held in India) between 15 and 20 September 2024 risk having their university admission cancelled.

European universities may not refund tuition fees until the student submits a letter from the embassy stating the reason for visa refusal, and even when they refund they usually deduct 30 to 40 percent.
The writer gives an illustrative average tuition payment of 4 lakh taka per student, so 100 students would have paid about 4 crore taka; many are from low or middle income families.

During the July 2024 unrest banks were closed, so many students turned to Bangladeshi expatriates and Bangladeshi students at foreign universities to pay tuition fees on their behalf or to get deadlines extended.
By Aug 2024 most embassies in Bangladesh, including those of the US, UK, Italy, Germany and Denmark, had resumed normal operations.

The writer says workers going to these European countries are also affected: if they cannot travel after getting a company job offer, job opportunities for Bangladeshis there may shrink; recruitment of Bangladeshi workers has become irregular in many countries.

headline_en: The full story of expatriates' movement for a new Bangladesh
summary_en: A Hamburg-based Bangladeshi, Rabiul H Chowdhury, describes diaspora protests in Germany and worldwide in July-August 2024, including a campaign not to send remittances. He notes that 57 Bangladeshis were convicted in the UAE over protests and voices long-standing expatriate grievances: little help from embassies, passport services, high Biman fares and airport mismanagement.

facts.statement: Bangladeshis in Hamburg, Germany held a protest rally on 18 Jul 2024 after obtaining German police permission on 17 Jul; protests also took place in Berlin, Munich, Cologne, Paris, London and New York.
During the July 2024 movement, expatriate Bangladeshis ran a campaign not to send remittances, which spread quickly; a diaspora team was formed to analyse the effect of not sending remittances.
57 Bangladeshis were convicted in the United Arab Emirates over protests linked to the 2024 movement.

The writer says expatriates have long been angry with the state: Bangladesh embassies rarely help them, there is little support from passport-making onwards, no special arrangement for workers in the Middle East, Biman Bangladesh tickets are always more expensive, and the airport shows extreme mismanagement.

summary_en: At a human chain at the National Press Club on 11 Aug 2024, Bangladesh Probashi Odhikar Oikko Parishad demanded the foreign ministry secure the release of Bangladeshis detained abroad for protesting in support of the anti-discrimination student movement. Speakers said more than a hundred were detained worldwide, 60 of them in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Qatar.

facts.statement: Speakers at a human chain in Dhaka on 11 Aug 2024 said more than a hundred expatriate Bangladeshis were detained in various countries for their role in the movement to topple the Sheikh Hasina government, and 60 were arrested in the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia and Qatar alone.
facts.source_in_article: Leaders of Bangladesh Probashi Odhikar Oikko Parishad

facts.statement: Bangladesh Probashi Odhikar Oikko Parishad demanded that the foreign ministry arrange the release of the detained migrants within one week (adviser Faruk Hasan).

Parishad leader Sultan Sarkar, himself based in Iraq, said migrants' lives had become unbearable due to embassy officials' indifference and asked the interim government to remove accused officials and appoint new ones.

headline_en: Chief Adviser to speak for release of convicted Bangladeshis
summary_en: Foreign Adviser M Touhid Hossain said on 11 Aug 2024 that Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus would speak to the UAE's highest level for release of Bangladeshi workers jailed for protesting in support of the student movement. On 22 Jul 2024 an Abu Dhabi court sentenced 57 Bangladeshis: 3 to life, 53 to 10 years and 1 to 11 years.

facts.statement: On 22 Jul 2024 a court in Abu Dhabi sentenced 57 Bangladeshis for street protests in solidarity with the anti-discrimination student movement: 3 to life imprisonment, 53 to 10 years each and 1 to 11 years.
In the UAE, Bangladeshi workers who joined street protests were not only detained but tried and jailed, according to Bangladesh's Foreign Adviser.

On 11 Aug 2024 Foreign Adviser M Touhid Hossain said Chief Adviser Dr Muhammad Yunus had promised to speak to the UAE's highest level within a day or two to seek the workers' release without punishment, after which the government would give them further support.

headline_en: Offshore banking pays higher profit: how to open an account
summary_en: Bangladeshis living abroad can open foreign-currency offshore (international banking) accounts in Bangladeshi banks from abroad, or a close relative can open one on their behalf. Banks pay up to 8.75% a year, tax-free under the Offshore Banking Act 2024, with no questions on source of funds and full repatriation allowed. About USD 50 million had been deposited, USD 24 million at City Bank alone (printed 22 Jul 2024).

facts.statement: A Bangladeshi living abroad can open a foreign-currency account (offshore banking or international banking account) in a Bangladeshi bank from abroad, or a close relative in Bangladesh can open it on their behalf; Bangladesh Bank allowed this at the end of 2023 amid the dollar crisis.

To open an offshore banking account from abroad, the expatriate applies through the bank's website and submits Bangladeshi citizenship information, proof of residence abroad, a work ID card and a photo; if someone in Bangladesh will operate the account, that person's details must also be submitted.

When a close relative in Bangladesh opens the offshore account on behalf of an expatriate, papers proving the relationship and information on the relative must be submitted, and both must submit ID, photos and other documents; details are found by searching 'offshore banking account' or 'international banking account' on the bank's website.
Banks offering offshore banking accounts to expatriates include The City Bank, BRAC Bank, Dutch-Bangla Bank, Pubali Bank, Eastern Bank and Islami Bank, among others.
Bangladesh Bank sets the maximum profit on offshore banking accounts; banks were paying up to 8.75% a year in July 2024, compared with up to 8% at foreign banks.
Profit earned on offshore banking accounts is fully income-tax-free; by contrast, income from deposits in taka accounts is taxed 15% without a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and 10% with a TIN.

Under the Offshore Banking Act 2024, no agency questions the source of money deposited in an offshore account, and the depositor can take the full amount with profit back to the country where they live at any time.
About USD 50 million or more had been deposited in offshore banking accounts in Bangladesh by July 2024, of which USD 24 million at The City Bank alone.

Bangladesh Bank's 2024 monetary policy said offshore banking, foreign-currency accounts for returnees and higher remittances would ease pressure on the exchange rate and raise reserves; MDs of several banks travelled abroad to promote international banking accounts to expatriates.

headline_en: May the ministry's initiatives succeed
summary_en: Editorial (24 Jul 2024): during the quota-movement unrest and curfew, three airlines cancelled 17 international flights over Friday to Sunday, stranding migrants at Shahjalal airport and nearby hotels at inflated prices. Saudi Airlines cancelled all flights on 19-20 July (1,200 passengers on four flights), and some workers' visas were due to expire in 2-7 days. The expatriates' welfare ministry said it was discussing a 15-day visa extension with the Saudi embassy; the aviation minister said efforts were under way to send them on Biman.

facts.statement: Over Friday, Saturday and Sunday (19-21 Jul 2024), three airlines cancelled 17 international flights from Dhaka; migrants who had spent several times the normal cost to reach Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport were stuck at the airport, unable to fly or return home under curfew, and many stayed in hotels near the Hajj Camp paying several times the normal room rent.

All Saudi Airlines flights were cancelled on 19 and 20 July 2024; 1,200 passengers were booked on four of those flights, and airlines could not say when flights would leave; many workers' visas had only 2 to 7 days left, putting their travel to Saudi Arabia at risk.
facts.source_in_article: Daily Bonik Barta, cited in editorial

facts.statement: Flights to Malaysia and other destinations were similarly disrupted in July 2024.
The Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare said it had discussed with the Saudi embassy extending by 15 days the visas of workers whose visas would expire during the flight disruption.

After visiting Shahjalal airport on Monday 22 Jul 2024, Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister Muhammad Faruk Khan said efforts were under way to send stranded Saudi-bound migrants to Saudi Arabia on Biman.
facts.source_in_article: Civil Aviation Minister Muhammad Faruk Khan

facts.statement: The editorial warns that if visas are not extended, many migrants may lose their jobs.

facts.statement: On 15 Jul 2024 Foreign Minister Hasan Mahmud met Saudi Ambassador Essa Youssef Essa Al-Duhailan; they discussed foreign office consultations, a joint Bangladesh-Saudi Arabia task force to protect Bangladeshis who want to go to Saudi Arabia for jobs from fraud, registration of businesses in Bangladeshis' own names in Saudi Arabia, and Saudi investment on 300 acres at Mirsarai, Chattogram.

headline_en: Chance to win up to one lakh taka receiving remittance in bKash via TapTap Send
summary_en: TapTap Send and bKash ran a campaign from 8 Jul to 30 Sep 2024 giving bonuses to recipients of the highest remittances into bKash accounts: up to 1 lakh taka monthly and 5,000 taka weekly for 10 people. TapTap Send lets migrants in 15 countries send any amount to bKash without charge, with the government's 2.5% incentive credited.

facts.statement: International money transfer company TapTap Send lets expatriates in 15 countries, including the US, UK, Italy, France, Canada, UAE, Portugal, Germany, Spain, the Netherlands, Belgium, Ireland and Austria, send any amount of remittance to a relative's bKash account in Bangladesh at no cost.
Remittances sent legally through TapTap Send arrive instantly in the recipient's bKash account via the banking channel along with the government incentive of 25 taka per 1,000 taka.

A joint TapTap Send and bKash campaign ran from 8 Jul to 30 Sep 2024: each month one recipient of the highest remittance in bKash could get up to 1 lakh taka bonus, and each week the 10 highest recipients got 5,000 taka each.

To qualify for the TapTap Send-bKash bonus, the expatriate had to send at least two remittances of 10,000 taka or more each to the relative's bKash account; a recipient could win the 1 lakh bonus once during the campaign, and weekly bonuses once a month and at most three times in three months; winners received bonuses within 3-4 working days after the week ended.

headline_en: Rishi's party sees landslide Labour victory coming
summary_en: Analysis on the eve of the July 2024 UK election. It notes Labour leader Keir Starmer said his government would return so-called illegal migrants to their countries soon after taking power, citing Bangladeshis as an example, and the Bangladesh High Commission wrote to him that no Bangladeshi entered the UK illegally by boat and Bangladesh is not in the top 20 countries of illegal migrants.

facts.statement: Before the 4 Jul 2024 UK election, Labour leader Keir Starmer said his government would send so-called illegal migrants back to their countries immediately after taking power, citing Bangladeshis as an example; shadow cabinet member Ashworth made the same remark the same day.

The Bangladesh High Commission in London wrote to Keir Starmer stating that no Bangladeshi had entered the UK illegally by boat and that Bangladesh is not in the list of the top 20 countries of illegal migrants to the UK.
More than 6% of voters in Keir Starmer's constituency are Bangladeshi.

headline_en: Work while studying abroad: these five countries can be destinations
summary_en: Feature (Jul 2024) based on ApplyBoard's chief experience officer Karun Kandoi, listing Australia, Canada, the UK, Ireland and the US as study destinations with part-time work rights. It gives weekly work-hour limits, post-study work periods and Australia's 2022-23 student visa numbers.

facts.statement: In Australia's 2022-23 financial year, student visas were granted to more than 166,000 of a total 179,000 applications; student visa approval rates rose to a record to fill post-Covid skill and financial gaps.
facts.source_in_article: Feature citing Education.com and India Today

facts.statement: In Australia, student visa holders' work limit was raised from the earlier 20 hours a week to 24 hours a week (after the Covid-era removal of the limit ended).
Australia's 485 Temporary Graduate visa was extended: bachelor's graduates can stay 4 years instead of 2, master's graduates 5 years instead of 3, and doctoral graduates 6 years.

In Canada, international students do not need a work permit for part-time work on or off campus; they can work 20 hours a week during their academic programme and full time during academic breaks, and after graduation can apply for the Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP).

In the UK, full-time international students may work up to 20 hours a week during studies and during course breaks or as part of academic placements; after graduating, the UK allows work on a graduate work visa for up to two years.

In Ireland, students can work part time up to 20 hours a week during studies and up to 40 hours a week during summer and winter holidays, which requires valid immigration Stamp 2; after graduation international students may work for 12 to 24 months.
In the US, international students on F-1 or M-1 visas get work opportunities under certain conditions, and some institutions offer government-approved on-campus jobs.
A survey cited in the feature says four of every five students are interested in studying in Canada.

summary_en: A banker's column on the 2024-25 budget, mainly about the absence of any mention of defaulted loans. It also criticises the budget decision to tax remittances sent to anyone other than spouse, children or parents, warning it may reduce remittances through legal channels.

The columnist warns the tax on remittances to relatives outside spouse, children and parents may reduce remittances through legal channels, because a significant share of remittances comes via other relatives.
The 2024-25 budget said introducing the 'crawling peg' exchange-rate method would increase remittances and export income.

headline_en: Women trafficked to India with promises of higher-paid jobs
summary_en: Chattogram police arrested Md. Tarek (34) on 24 Jun 2024 in a case filed by a trafficked woman. His wife Jhumu Akter befriended laid-off women garment workers and lured them with higher-paid parlour jobs in India; they were taken across the Jashore border to hotels in Jharkhand and forced into sex work. The complainant and a friend crossed on 2 June and later escaped.

facts.statement: Jhumu Akter, wife of Md. Tarek, befriended women garment workers in Chattogram factories, especially those who had lost their jobs, and lured them with offers of higher-paid work in beauty parlours in India.
facts.source_in_article: OC Sanjoy Kumar Sinha, Bayezid Bostami police station

facts.statement: The complainant and a friend went with Tarek to Jashore on 29 May 2024; about six kilometres on they saw the India-Bangladesh border barbed-wire fence, were kept in a house beside the border, and on 2 June were taken across the fence to a hotel in Jharkhand state, India.
Women trafficked to Jharkhand, India via the Jashore border were confined in hotels and forced into sex work, and tortured if they refused.

On Monday 24 Jun 2024 police arrested Md. Tarek (34) at Chandranagar, Bayezid Bostami thana, Chattogram, in a trafficking case filed by a victim naming Tarek, his wife Jhumu Akter, associate Anisur Rahman and 3-4 unnamed people; police said Tarek confessed under interrogation.

headline_en: Government has 'Russell's vipers' but no mongoose to catch them: Sayedul Haque
summary_en: Report on the 24 Jun 2024 budget debate in parliament. Expatriates' Welfare State Minister Shafiqur Rahman Chowdhury said a six-member committee was probing the situation of workers who had permission but could not go to Malaysia, over 3,000 complaints had been received, those responsible would face legal action and affected workers would be compensated.

facts.statement: Expatriates' Welfare State Minister Shafiqur Rahman Chowdhury told parliament on 24 Jun 2024 that measures would be taken to compensate Bangladeshis who had received permission but could not go to Malaysia.

A six-member inquiry committee was formed over the Malaysia worker-sending situation; workers who had the required papers but could not go to Malaysia were asked to file complaints with the committee, and more than 3,000 complaints had been received by 24 Jun 2024.

The State Minister said the inquiry committee would verify the complaints and appropriate legal action would be taken against those really responsible for creating the situation in which workers could not go to Malaysia.

headline_en: Thoughts on the journey to Medina
summary_en: A Hajj travel feature on the Mecca-Medina road. It quotes a Bangladeshi migrant, Sekandar, working at the Sasco rest stop, who said he spent over 2 lakh taka to come to Saudi Arabia, and describes the road and passport checks on entering Medina.

facts.statement: Sekandar, a Bangladeshi migrant met at the Sasco rest stop on the Mecca-Medina road in Saudi Arabia, said he spent more than 2 lakh taka from Bangladesh to come to Saudi Arabia.
facts.source_in_article: Sekandar, Bangladeshi migrant in Saudi Arabia

facts.statement: Sekandar said traffic at the Mecca-Medina rest stops is heaviest in the Hajj months of Zilqad and Zilhajj, during Umrah, Ramadan, and on Thursdays and Fridays.

The Mecca-Medina road is a 423 km four-lane one-way highway taking about six hours with a 120 km/h speed limit; on entering Medina, Hajj buses stop at a Saudi government office where passports and related papers are checked.
The writer advises noting your vehicle's number when getting off at roadside rest stops in Saudi Arabia, because many vehicles of the same look and colour may be parked when you return.

headline_en: 49 Rohingyas given birth registration in Dhaka North City
summary_en: Dhaka North City Corporation's health department issued birth registrations to 49 Rohingyas, which the Registrar General has suspended in the BDRIS system. Police Special Branch had reported on 26 May 2024 that 102 Rohingyas obtained birth registration illegally through broker rings, dishonest officials and local representatives and then got Bangladeshi passports with false permanent addresses.

facts.statement: Police Special Branch wrote to the Registrar General of Birth and Death Registration on 26 May 2024 that 102 people, Rohingya citizens of Myanmar, had obtained birth registration illegally from various places through broker rings, dishonest officials and staff, and local public representatives, and had then made Bangladeshi passports; the permanent addresses in their passports were found to be false.

On 5 Jun 2024 the Registrar General's office wrote to Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) that 49 Rohingyas' birth registrations issued by DNCC were illegal and had been suspended in the BDRIS system; the registrars and assistants responsible must explain within 5 working days or face legal action.

Of 77 names Prothom Alo obtained from the Special Branch list of 102, 42 got birth registration from DNCC zonal offices: 9 from Zone-2, 17 from Zone-3, 14 from Zone-4, and one each from Zone-5 and Zone-9.

In February 2023 DNCC dismissed birth-death registration assistant Mafruza Sultana (Zone-5) and suspended assistant health officer Azizun Nesa (Zone-3) for birth registration fraud; Azizun Nesa was later reinstated. In April 2023 birth certificates were again issued to a South Korean national and a Rohingya, with no action taken.

headline_en: 5 Bangladeshis released on bail in Spain
summary_en: Five Bangladeshi sailors detained since March 2020 on suspicion of involvement in smuggling drugs from Colombia to Spain on the ship MV Karar were released on conditional bail from Alama (Pontevedra) prison on 24 Apr 2024. The Bangladesh embassy in Madrid said it had pressed Spanish authorities for a speedy hearing.

facts.statement: Spain's coast guard detained five Bangladeshi sailors and 19 other foreign sailors of the ship MV Karar on suspicion of involvement in smuggling drugs from Colombia to Spain; on 20 Mar 2020 the Vigo provincial court ordered them held in interim custody pending further investigation, and the custody was prolonged as the investigation and trial dragged on.

On 24 Apr 2024 the Vigo provincial court released the five Bangladeshis (Alimullah, Mohammad Altaf Hossain, Mohammed Imran Sharif, Md. Ataur Rahman and Mahfuzul Haque) on bail from Alama central prison, Pontevedra, on condition they attend future hearings and do not leave Spain.

The Bangladesh embassy in Spain monitored the case and contacted Spanish ministries several times asking for a speedy hearing and release; the five met Ambassador Mohammad Sarwar Mahmood at the embassy on 4 Jun 2024 and thanked it for consular service.

headline_en: Five Bangladeshis released on bail in Spain
summary_en: The Bangladesh embassy in Madrid said on 5 Jun 2024 that five Bangladeshi sailors held in Alama central prison, Pontevedra, since 2020 on suspicion of drug smuggling on the ship MV Karar were granted conditional bail by the Vigo provincial court on 24 Apr 2024. Conditions: attend future hearings and not leave Spain before final bail.

facts.statement: On 24 Apr 2024 the Vigo provincial court in Spain granted bail to five Bangladeshi sailors (Alimullah, Mohammad Altaf Hossain, Mohammed Imran Sharif, Md. Ataur Rahman, Mahfuzul Haque) held in Alama central prison, Pontevedra, on two conditions: they must appear at the Vigo court at future hearings, and they cannot leave Spain before getting final bail.

Spain's coast guard detained the five Bangladeshi sailors and 19 other foreign sailors on suspicion of involvement in smuggling drugs from Colombia to Spain on the ship MV Karar; after a preliminary hearing a judge ordered interim custody on 20 Mar 2020 and further investigation, and custody grew longer as the case dragged on.

The Bangladesh embassy in Madrid monitored the case and contacted Spanish ministries several times seeking a speedy hearing, justice and release; the five visited the embassy on 4 Jun 2024 and met Ambassador Mohammad Sarwar Mahmood.

headline_en: People want to see what action government takes against 4 MPs of Malaysia 'syndicate': Nurul
summary_en: At a 4 Jun 2024 rally by Bangladesh Sramik Odhikar Parishad demanding arrest of those who took thousands of crores from Malaysia-bound workers and compensation for victims, Gono Odhikar Parishad president Nurul Haque named four MPs reported as linked to the Malaysia syndicate. He said the Malaysian labour market had closed three times under this government because of the syndicate.

facts.statement: Gono Odhikar Parishad president Nurul Haque said four MPs had been named in the media as linked to the Malaysia recruitment syndicate: former finance minister Mustafa Kamal, Nizam Hazari of Feni, Benzir Ahmed of Dhaka and Jatiya Party MP Masud Uddin; he said the former finance minister had brought his wife and daughter into the manpower business.
Nurul Haque said the Malaysian labour market had closed three times under the Awami League government because of the syndicate.

Bangladesh Sramik Odhikar Parishad held a rally at the National Press Club on 4 Jun 2024 demanding the arrest of those in the ring that took thousands of crores of taka from Malaysia-bound workers through fraud, and compensation for victims.
Nurul Haque said the labour market in the Middle East was also in crisis and that opportunities for Bangladeshi imams in the Middle East were not being used due to government incompetence.

Overall I am very satisfied with what I saw: aviation minister
summary_en: Aviation Minister Muhammad Faruk Khan, inspecting Shahjalal airport's third terminal (97% complete) on 30 May 2024, said baggage now takes 15 minutes for the first bag and about 40 for the last. On Malaysia airfares, he said those sending workers knew a month ahead that 31 May was the deadline but recruiting agencies did not act; Biman was running 3-4 daily flights to Malaysia and a charter on Air Cambodia had been approved.

facts.statement: Aviation Minister Muhammad Faruk Khan said on 30 May 2024 that those involved in sending workers to Malaysia knew a month earlier that 31 May 2024 was the last date for sending workers, but recruiting agencies and other suppliers did not make arrangements.

Before the 31 May 2024 Malaysia deadline, Biman was operating three to four flights a day to Malaysia; on 29 May some people from Malaysia sought and got same-day permission for a chartered Air Cambodia flight from Dhaka to Malaysia.

At Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, the first checked bag currently takes about 15 minutes and the last about 40 minutes to arrive; the third terminal was 97% complete with no opening date given.

headline_en: Support for exports and remittances should be increased
summary_en: Former Bangladesh Bank governor Atiur Rahman said at an AmCham event on 26 May 2024 that tax breaks and cash incentives for exports and remittances should continue for several more years and even be increased. He also said the decision to float the exchange rate came a year late.

facts.statement: Former Bangladesh Bank governor Atiur Rahman said on 26 May 2024 that tax breaks or cash incentives on remittances (and exports) should continue for several more years regardless of what the international community says, and that subsidies in these sectors should be increased.
